definitions.explanation: The confusion or surprise a person feels on meeting a culture, custom or way of thinking very different from their own, typically when living abroad. Also used loosely for any surprising difference between groups.

examples.japanese: カルチャーショック⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{受|う}けた→受ける：01215_ukeru⟧。
⟦{留学|りゅうがく}→留学：03677_ryuugaku⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{最初|さいしょ}→最初：00882_saisho⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{一か月|いっかげつ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧カルチャーショック⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{連続|れんぞく}→連続：03783_renzoku⟧だった。
examples.english: My first month studying abroad was one culture shock after another.

examples.japanese: ⟦{東京|とうきょう}→東京：09564_toukyou⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{田舎|いなか}→田舎：01320_inaka⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}して→引っ越す：01171_hikkosu⟧、⟦{近所|きんじょ}→近所：01318_kinjo⟧づきあい⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{濃|こ}さ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧カルチャーショック⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{受|う}けた→受ける：01215_ukeru⟧。
examples.english: When I moved from Tokyo to the countryside, the closeness of neighborhood ties came as a culture shock.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- カルチャーショック⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{受|う}ける→受ける：01215_ukeru⟧: to experience culture shock
- カルチャーショック⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じる→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧: to feel culture shock
- ⟦{逆|ぎゃく}→逆：02649_gyaku⟧カルチャーショック: reverse culture shock (on returning home)

USAGE:
As in English, it is often used jokingly for small surprises inside one country, such as differences between regions, generations or workplaces.
